name: A thermostat switching a heater
description:
A room losing heat to 5 °C outside, with a time constant of two hours, and a heater that warms it at 10 °C an hour, switched by a thermostat with a dead band: on when the room falls through 19 °C, off when it rises through 21 °C. Between switches the room follows Newton's law of cooling. At each switch the right-hand side jumps, and the solver has to stop exactly there rather than step across it.

Too_cold and Too_warm are the two triggers. Each takes a snapshot of the time it fires (On_since, Off_since), and the heater is on while On_since is the later of the two: a memory of which way the room last crossed, made of two snapshots.

The switching times are known in closed form. Warming from 15 to 21 °C takes τ·ln(10/4) = 1.83 h; after that each cycle is τ·ln(16/14) = 0.27 h with the heater off and τ·ln(6/4) = 0.81 h with it on, 42 switches in the day. The run lands on every one of them to within half a millisecond.
